lessons.title: నలుపు, తెలుపు, ఎరుపు, నీలం — the pattern completes itself
lessons.gloss: black, white, red, blue — Telugu's own basic colors, completing the whole family's shared blue

segments.text: By now the shape should feel familiar: native colors for black, white, and red — and one shared Sanskrit word for blue. Telugu confirms it a fourth time.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: Three native colors
The word, taken apart - The same shared blue, one more time

segments.text: నీలం (nīlam) = "blue" — the identical Sanskrit నీల (nīla) loan that also sits in Tamil (nīlam), Malayalam (nīla), Kannada (nīli), and Hindi (nīlā). Four Dravidian languages plus Hindi, all independently keeping their own native black/white/red, and all reaching for the exact same borrowed word the moment it comes to blue.

segments.source: [YOU SAY: "nalupu, telupu, erupu" — black, white, red]

segments.instruction: "nīlam" — blue, the word the four Dravidian languages and Hindi all share
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "nīlam" — blue, the word the four Dravidian languages and Hindi all share]

segments.instruction: the whole pattern, one more time — native, native, native, borrowed
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the whole pattern, one more time — native, native, native, **borrowed**]

segments.text: What's the pattern across Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, and Telugu's basic colors? (Black, white, and red are native Dravidian words in every one of them; blue is a shared Sanskrit loan (nīla) in every one of them.)
